verdict.rationale: Keycloak is itself an OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect authorization server. Its docs cover registering client applications, including a dynamic client registration endpoint, and publish a well-known discovery endpoint. They also document token issuance via client credentials and device grants, plus introspection and revocation endpoints, and community users confirm it exposes a clean OAuth 2.0/OIDC interface to many apps. It runs as a separate server fronting your app rather than inside it. missing for 10: no evidence of user consent screens for third-party clients, no hands-on corroboration specific to issuing tokens to external third-party developers.
